We examine the ease with which the "very simplest" scoto-se seesaw model (where "scoto-" signifies that seesaw mechanisms involving off-diagonal neutrino mass terms rely on new physics) accounts for Higgs boson mass, three known active neutrino mass eigenvalues, two 95 GeV scalar dark matter particles, and one 1.5 TeV WIMP dark matter particle. Our "three-neutrino plus two-new-neutrin" (3n+2NN) framework predicts light neutrino seescaling, Higgs mass generation, light dark sector neutrinos, and heavy WIMPs via additional radiative corrections. The model achieves this via the addition of two new right-handed (RH) and two new scalar singlet fields to the Standard Model (SM). The three scalar mass eigenvalues result from mixing between new diagonalized terms and existing off-diagonal entries in the mass matrix. We analyze the radiative stability requirements for both the Higgs and three-light-dark-sector masses, focusing on loop corrections involving WIMP interactions. The model predicts two new scalar singlet fields, one-WIMP, and one-neutrino masses, which are all experimentally accessible. The 3n+2NN framework unifies WIMP, light-dark-sector, and experimental-hierarchy explanations within a single theoretical structure.
